title: Cortical pair orientation gave no clear slice-held-out delay prediction gain in four Allen mouse and human groups
abstract: We tested whether cortical pair orientation adds information about synaptic delay beyond soma distance, image-plane separation, cell class, and layer. We used 1,839 connected pairs from Allen Synaptic Physiology r2.1 small. Four groups separate mouse and human records and excitatory and inhibitory synapses. Five-fold tests held out whole slices. Adding vertical orientation did not give a clear decrease in mean absolute log error in any group at ridge penalty 10. All four slice-bootstrap intervals included zero. Adjusted full-sample slopes were negative for excitatory pairs in both species. These associations did not establish useful prediction across slices. The test uses selected brain-slice recordings. Slice groups can share a donor. The small human inhibitory group and missing geometry limit the result.
